title: The gate behind the generic export refusal, named on the shipped runtime
question: EXP-047 and EXP-048 recorded graceful stops that refused to save live sessions with the generic `program refused continuation export`. Which gate refuses, and why?
answer: The two refused sessions were the two 126K-token sessions, and their engine continuations had already been evicted: every save at the end - explicit, automatic and shutdown - stopped at the engine gate `session is not indexed in the engine`. While they were resident, each automatic save attempt hit a transient gate and was dropped, not retried: `catalogued checkpoint tag mismatch` 1 ms after a turn completed (the save ran before the new continuation was catalogued), then `resource transaction in progress` while the next request ran. The 67.7K-token fanout session that arrived next evicted both. The store had been overwriting each of these named engine gates with the generic program refusal.

conclusion: Nothing is wrong with the exporter itself: when a continuation is resident and quiescent it exports (5.2 GB fanout session in 4.3 s, agent session in 0.7 s). Sessions are lost because the automatic save drops transient refusals instead of retrying them, and eviction under host-KV pressure then removes the only exportable copy. Two fixes follow: retry transient automatic refusals (tag mismatch before catalog publication, transaction in progress) when the engine quiesces; and save a continuation whose checkpoint is behind before it is evicted, as restore reclaim already saves a stale resident before reclaiming it.
limits: One reproduction on the RTX 5090 lane with a back-to-back workload that leaves no idle gap between turns; interactive use has gaps in which a retried automatic save would run.
Successful automatic saves are not logged, so this receipt cannot show whether D1 or D2 had an earlier generation on disk; the shutdown reported both as unsaved at their latest response.
The RTX 4090 native lane builds from the same source and was not reproduced here.
